text:
Given recent events, I wouldn't be surprised to see consensus shift (or strengthen?) to ETFs being the best place to gain hassle-free exposure to BTC, ironically.   

I don't think this is necessarily wrong from a risk pov, especially for the average person. Though, each option does come with its own set of risks. ETFs hold third party risk, while self-custody holds individual technical risk. A balance of the two might be the way forward for most.

An interesting thought experiment - imagine if a portion of the ETF bitcoins were lost, say, due to an institutional custodian losing the keys to all or some of the holdings, sending bitcoin prices astronomically higher, while you are affected and unable to take part in the upside ... would be brutal. 

This seems unlikely, but I think such thought experiments are worth while, especially given what we've seen in our industry over the years. Either way, it's always worth questioning your setup from an adversarial perspective and truly understanding your risk exposure, from as many angles as you can ...

text:
Current bias / thought process dump

Before this pamp, I was leaning towards a final low into 44-49k for BTC, and the 2025 low being taken on ETH.

However, many alts were looking bottomed (covered CRV over the months, for example). 

Being pretty certain on CRV having bottomed AND leaning towards BTC due another low, my overall lean was something like this:

- CRV rallies up into major supply around 0.35-0.39 (with other alts pushing too)

- BTC and ETH move up to range highs 

- Final market wipe, BTC revisits 59k for a triple tap OR lower low into 44-49k

- Alts retrace for a *higher low*

Thus, my two lanes of thinking could co-exist 

This MIGHT still happen. However, I’ll admit this move up seems pretty aggressive on BTC and ETH, so I’m willing to concede once weekly and monthly candles close bullish. Then we can enjoy a push to 100-110k for the next decision point.

> Missing the bottom is fine.

> Not switching bias when the charts tell you otherwise, is not. 

Either way, this volatility across crypto is refreshing. Next couple of weeks will be very telling.

GL 🤝

text:
It’s funny. When I think about trading these last *checks notes* 9 years it’s interesting how often you can get psyoped into a certain narrative and how much stress that adds to trading decisions.

Don’t fall for it. 

Just try and buy perceived discount when things seem cheap. And sell perceived premium when things seem expensive.

I say perceived because I can’t tell you to buy the bottom and sell the top. No one can do that. It’s simply down to how you interpret the market. Point is, remove all the noise, “muh narrative”, the headlines, and most of all, the rollercoaster takes on CT. 

Strip it all down to the bare bones. Operate from a place of calm and clarity. And ask yourself, do you even have a system? Or are you just smashing buttons and hoping for the best - that’s one way to financial ruin. But the other way really doesn’t have to be too complicated. 

Anyway, just some random thoughts …
